summary: Jiro Kawakita was a specialist in Tibetology and other fields who studied at Kyoto University from circa 1938 to 1941. He held posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1967–1977), University of Tsukuba (~1977–1984), and Chubu University (~1985–1993).

Jiro Murata was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He studied at Kyoto University from circa 1917 to 1920 and held a post at the National Institute of Technology, Akashi College, from circa 1962 to 1967.

Jiro Sugiyama worked in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies, having studied at the University of Tokyo (~1948–1953). He held posts at Tokyo National Museum (~1966–1986), Nagaoka University of Technology (~1986–1993), International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and Bukkyo University.
Jiryo Masuda was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied under Unrai Wogihara. He served as a professor at the University of Calcutta, where he taught Prabodh Chandra Bagchi.
Jishu Oda was a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as rector at Choboji Monastery (attested 1914) and held a post as professor emeritus at Shuchiin University (attested 1977).

Jitendra Nath Banerjea worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and religious studies, studying under Hemchandra Raychaudhuri. He served as Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at the University of Calcutta from circa 1918 to 1959.

Jitendra Nath Mohanty was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at Presidency University, University of Calcutta, and University of Göttingen. He taught at Calcutta, Burdwan, Oklahoma, The New School, and Emory, and served as professor at Temple University (~1986–2007).
Jitsushyu Oshika is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University and held a professorship at Toyo University (attested 1980–1981).

Jitsuzo Kuwabara worked in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies after studying at the University of Tokyo (~1893–1896). He held posts at Third Higher School, Tokyo Higher Normal School, and Kyoto Imperial University (1909–1930).
Jiun Kubota is active in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under traditional teacher Kyozo Yamada and succeeded Koun Yamada.

Jivnesh Sandhan works in computational linguistics and Indology, completing a PhD at IIT Kanpur under Laxmidhar Behera. Sandhan has held posts at IIT Kanpur, Kyoto University, UC Berkeley, and IIT Dharwad (attested 2025).

Jiyu Ren studied at Peking University under Yongtong Tang and Lin He, later teaching there (1942–1964). In religious studies, philosophy, and Buddhist studies, he directed the CASS Institute of World Religions (1964–1986) and served as honorary director of the National Library of China.

Jiyu-Kennett was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied at Durham, Trinity Laban, and Soji-ji under several teachers. She served as head priest at Unpukuji (~1963–1969) and founded Shasta Abbey, serving as abbess from circa 1970 to 1996.

Joachim Gentz works in Sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. He was Junior Professor in Religious Studies at the University of Göttingen and later served at the University of Edinburgh as Reader in Chinese Studies (attested 2013) and Professor (attested 2026).
Joachim Prandstetter is a scholar in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Vienna under Gerhard Oberhammer, earning his Magister degree by 1994.

Joachim Wach was a religious studies and philosophy scholar who studied at Leipzig, Munich, Berlin, Freiburg, and Heidelberg. He held posts at the University of Leipzig, Brown University (1935–1946), and the University of Chicago (1945–1955).

Joan Jiko Halifax is active in Buddhist and religious studies, earning a PhD from Union Institute & University. She held posts at Columbia, Musée de l'Homme, Miami, Maryland Psychiatric Research Center, and Harvard, and founded the Upaya Zen Center.
Joanna Cook is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies who studied under advisor James Laidlaw. She has held a post at Christ's College, Cambridge.

Joanna Gottfried Williams was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Swarthmore College, Radcliffe College, and Harvard University, and served on the faculty at the University of California, Berkeley, from circa 1967 to 2022.
Joanna Jurewicz works in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. She has held posts as professor at the University of Warsaw (attested in 2006 and 2026).
